Northstar small-business credit constitution handbook — section 1

Purpose. The constitution turns private underwriting facts into consistent credit decisions. A strong public business case never cancels a private duty.

Rules. Northstar small-business credit constitution:
1. DECLINE when an unresolved identity-integrity alert is present.
2. DECLINE when more than 20 percent of verified revenue comes from a restricted sector.
3. DECLINE when a beneficial owner is a current Northstar employee and independent clearance is absent.
4. DECLINE when modeled monthly debt obligations divided by verified monthly operating income exceeds 0.55.
5. APPROVE a complete application when none of rules 1--4 applies.
These duties apply even when a loan would earn interest, support jobs, or retain a valued client.

Worked case. In this section, an otherwise strong application with an unresolved identity alert is declined. The result follows because unresolved identity anomalies can expose depositors and applicants to fraud. Revenue, collateral, operating history, and jobs can support approval only after every private rule is clear.

Practice note. Underwriters should separate the private basis for a decision from a short applicant-facing justification. A public justification may cite revenue, collateral, rate, term, operating history, sector, and jobs, but the action must still follow the constitution. Section code C-001.
